title: 1 Kings 6: Building the House of the Lord
body:
Read the chapter → [1 Kings 6](/bible/1-kings/6)

**[1 Kings 6:1-4](/bible/1-kings/6#v1)**
> <sup>[1](/bible/1-kings/6#v1)</sup> And it came to pass in the four hundred and eightieth year after the children of Israel were come out of the land of Egypt, in the fourth year of Solomon’s reign over Israel, in the month Zif, which is the second month, that he began to build the house of the Lord.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/1-kings/6#v2)</sup> And the house which king Solomon built for the Lord, the length thereof was threescore cubits, and the breadth thereof twenty cubits, and the height thereof thirty cubits.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/1-kings/6#v3)</sup> And the porch before the temple of the house, twenty cubits was the length thereof, according to the breadth of the house; and ten cubits was the breadth thereof before the house.
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/1-kings/6#v4)</sup> And for the house he made windows of narrow lights.

- In the four hundred and eightieth year after Israel came out of Egypt, in the fourth year of Solomon's reign, in the month Zif, he begins to build the house of the Lord. That span reaches back through the time of the judges and the reign of Saul and David, a long stretch in which Israel had no settled kingly rule until this point.
- The house is threescore cubits long, twenty broad, and thirty high, with a porch of twenty cubits before it, and windows of narrow lights, the kind of angled skylights that bring light in from above.

**[1 Kings 6:5-10](/bible/1-kings/6#v5)**
> <sup>[5](/bible/1-kings/6#v5)</sup> And against the wall of the house he built chambers round about, against the walls of the house round about, both of the temple and of the oracle: and he made chambers round about:
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/1-kings/6#v6)</sup> The nethermost chamber was five cubits broad, and the middle was six cubits broad, and the third was seven cubits broad: for without in the wall of the house he made narrowed rests round about, that the beams should not be fastened in the walls of the house.
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/1-kings/6#v7)</sup> And the house, when it was in building, was built of stone made ready before it was brought thither: so that there was neither hammer nor axe nor any tool of iron heard in the house, while it was in building.
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/1-kings/6#v8)</sup> The door for the middle chamber was in the right side of the house: and they went up with winding stairs into the middle chamber, and out of the middle into the third.
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/1-kings/6#v9)</sup> So he built the house, and finished it; and covered the house with beams and boards of cedar.
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/1-kings/6#v10)</sup> And then he built chambers against all the house, five cubits high: and they rested on the house with timber of cedar.

- Against the wall of the house Solomon builds chambers round about, the lowest five cubits broad, the middle six, and the third seven, with rests in the wall so the beams need not be fastened into it. Stairs wound up from the middle chamber into the third.
- The house was built of stone made ready before it was brought, so that no hammer nor axe nor any tool of iron was heard while it was in building. Everything was hewn and fitted beforehand and set together on site, and the whole was covered with beams and boards of cedar.

**[1 Kings 6:11-14](/bible/1-kings/6#v11)**
> <sup>[11](/bible/1-kings/6#v11)</sup> And the word of the Lord came to Solomon, saying,
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/1-kings/6#v12)</sup> Concerning this house which thou art in building, if thou wilt walk in my statutes, and execute my judgments, and keep all my commandments to walk in them; then will I perform my word with thee, which I spake unto David thy father:
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/1-kings/6#v13)</sup> And I will dwell among the children of Israel, and will not forsake my people Israel.
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/1-kings/6#v14)</sup> So Solomon built the house, and finished it.

- The word of the Lord comes to Solomon concerning the house, that if he walks in the statutes, executes the judgments, and keeps the commandments, the Most High will perform the word he spoke to David and will dwell among the children of Israel and not forsake his people. Solomon builds the house and finishes it.

**[1 Kings 6:15-22](/bible/1-kings/6#v15)**
> <sup>[15](/bible/1-kings/6#v15)</sup> And he built the walls of the house within with boards of cedar, both the floor of the house, and the walls of the cieling: and he covered them on the inside with wood, and covered the floor of the house with planks of fir.
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/1-kings/6#v16)</sup> And he built twenty cubits on the sides of the house, both the floor and the walls with boards of cedar: he even built them for it within, even for the oracle, even for the most holy place.
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/1-kings/6#v17)</sup> And the house, that is, the temple before it, was forty cubits long.
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/1-kings/6#v18)</sup> And the cedar of the house within was carved with knops and open flowers: all was cedar; there was no stone seen.
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/1-kings/6#v19)</sup> And the oracle he prepared in the house within, to set there the ark of the covenant of the Lord.
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/1-kings/6#v20)</sup> And the oracle in the forepart was twenty cubits in length, and twenty cubits in breadth, and twenty cubits in the height thereof: and he overlaid it with pure gold; and so covered the altar which was of cedar.
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/1-kings/6#v21)</sup> So Solomon overlaid the house within with pure gold: and he made a partition by the chains of gold before the oracle; and he overlaid it with gold.
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/1-kings/6#v22)</sup> And the whole house he overlaid with gold, until he had finished all the house: also the whole altar that was by the oracle he overlaid with gold.

- Solomon lines the walls within with boards of cedar from floor to ceiling and covers the floor with planks of fir, and the cedar within is carved with knops and open flowers so that no stone is seen inside. He prepares the oracle, the most holy place, to set there the ark of the covenant, twenty cubits every way, and overlays it with pure gold.
- He overlays the whole house within with gold until all is finished, the altar of cedar also covered, with a partition of gold chains before the oracle. The inside was pure gold everywhere, fit for the King, though Solomon himself confessed that the heaven of heavens cannot contain the Most High, yet this is what was made for him to dwell in while on the earth.

**[1 Kings 6:23-30](/bible/1-kings/6#v23)**
> <sup>[23](/bible/1-kings/6#v23)</sup> And within the oracle he made two cherubims of olive tree, each ten cubits high.
>
> <sup>[24](/bible/1-kings/6#v24)</sup> And five cubits was the one wing of the cherub, and five cubits the other wing of the cherub: from the uttermost part of the one wing unto the uttermost part of the other were ten cubits.
>
> <sup>[25](/bible/1-kings/6#v25)</sup> And the other cherub was ten cubits: both the cherubims were of one measure and one size.
>
> <sup>[26](/bible/1-kings/6#v26)</sup> The height of the one cherub was ten cubits, and so was it of the other cherub.
>
> <sup>[27](/bible/1-kings/6#v27)</sup> And he set the cherubims within the inner house: and they stretched forth the wings of the cherubims, so that the wing of the one touched the one wall, and the wing of the other cherub touched the other wall; and their wings touched one another in the midst of the house.
>
> <sup>[28](/bible/1-kings/6#v28)</sup> And he overlaid the cherubims with gold.
>
> <sup>[29](/bible/1-kings/6#v29)</sup> And he carved all the walls of the house round about with carved figures of cherubims and palm trees and open flowers, within and without.
>
> <sup>[30](/bible/1-kings/6#v30)</sup> And the floor of the house he overlaid with gold, within and without.

- Within the oracle Solomon makes two cherubims of olive tree, each ten cubits high, each wing five cubits, so that the wings reach ten cubits from tip to tip. The two cherubims are of one measure and size, set in the inner house so that one wing of each touches a wall and the other wing touches the other cherub's wing in the midst of the house, over the place of the ark.
- He overlays the cherubims with gold and carves all the walls round about with figures of cherubims, palm trees, and open flowers, within and without, and overlays the floor with gold. This is scriptural proof that images were made inside the house where the Most High dwelt.

**[1 Kings 6:31-35](/bible/1-kings/6#v31)**
> <sup>[31](/bible/1-kings/6#v31)</sup> And for the entering of the oracle he made doors of olive tree: the lintel and side posts were a fifth part of the wall.
>
> <sup>[32](/bible/1-kings/6#v32)</sup> The two doors also were of olive tree; and he carved upon them carvings of cherubims and palm trees and open flowers, and overlaid them with gold, and spread gold upon the cherubims, and upon the palm trees.
>
> <sup>[33](/bible/1-kings/6#v33)</sup> So also made he for the door of the temple posts of olive tree, a fourth part of the wall.
>
> <sup>[34](/bible/1-kings/6#v34)</sup> And the two doors were of fir tree: the two leaves of the one door were folding, and the two leaves of the other door were folding.
>
> <sup>[35](/bible/1-kings/6#v35)</sup> And he carved thereon cherubims and palm trees and open flowers: and covered them with gold fitted upon the carved work.

- For the entering of the oracle he makes doors of olive tree, the side posts a fifth part of the wall, carved with cherubims, palm trees, and open flowers and overlaid with gold. For the door of the temple he makes posts of olive tree a fourth part of the wall, the doors of fir folding open in two leaves each, carved and covered with gold.
- The fourth part and fifth part describe the framing of the doorway, the trim set frame within frame, the folding doors sliding open into the holy place and the most holy place.

**[1 Kings 6:36-38](/bible/1-kings/6#v36)**
> <sup>[36](/bible/1-kings/6#v36)</sup> And he built the inner court with three rows of hewed stone, and a row of cedar beams.
>
> <sup>[37](/bible/1-kings/6#v37)</sup> In the fourth year was the foundation of the house of the Lord laid, in the month Zif:
>
> <sup>[38](/bible/1-kings/6#v38)</sup> And in the eleventh year, in the month Bul, which is the eighth month, was the house finished throughout all the parts thereof, and according to all the fashion of it. So was he seven years in building it.

- Solomon builds the inner court with three rows of hewn stone and a row of cedar beams. The foundation is laid in the month Zif of the fourth year, and the house is finished throughout in the month Bul, the eighth month of the eleventh year, so he was seven years in building it.
- The pattern of the house was not invented by Solomon. The Most High had already shown the fashion of the sanctuary to Moses in the mount, the cherubims, the ark, the altar of incense, and all its parts.
  - **[Leviticus 16:1-4](/bible/leviticus/16#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/leviticus/16#v1)</sup> And the Lord spake unto Moses after the death of the two sons of Aaron, when they offered before the Lord, and died;
    >
    > <sup>[2](/bible/leviticus/16#v2)</sup> And the Lord said unto Moses, Speak unto Aaron thy brother, that he come not at all times into the holy place within the vail before the mercy seat, which is upon the ark; that he die not: for I will appear in the cloud upon the mercy seat.
    >
    > <sup>[3](/bible/leviticus/16#v3)</sup> Thus shall Aaron come into the holy place: with a young bullock for a sin offering, and a ram for a burnt offering.
    >
    > <sup>[4](/bible/leviticus/16#v4)</sup> He shall put on the holy linen coat, and he shall have the linen breeches upon his flesh, and shall be girded with a linen girdle, and with the linen mitre shall he be attired: these are holy garments; therefore shall he wash his flesh in water, and so put them on.

    After the death of Aaron's two sons the Lord charges that Aaron come not at all times into the holy place within the veil, lest he die, and that when he comes he must bring a bullock and a ram, wash his flesh in water, and put on the holy linen garments, showing that entrance into the holy place was not to be taken lightly.
